english.title: Produce / give false document / information - immigration
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), with a view to obtaining

(A)_[for yourself]_
(B)_[for another, namely **(..SPECIFY PERSON..),]_

support under any provision made by or under Part VI of the Immigration and Asylum Act 1999, produced or gave to **(..SPECIFY PERSON..), a person exercising functions under Part VI of the Immigration and Asylum Act 1999, a document or information which you knew to be false in a material particular, namely **(..SPECIFY..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 105(1) and (2) of the Immigration and Asylum Act 1999.
english.pointstoprove:

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: See Section 95 for details for the provision of support for asylum-seekers/dependants of asylum seekers.

other.penalty:
Three months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
